newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SAKIC SCORES WITH SECOND IN REGULATION, SETS UP OT WINNER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SAKIC SCORES WITH SECOND IN REGULATION, SETS UP OT WINNER.

text.p: Joe Sakic scored the tying goal with one second left in regulation and set up Mike Ricci's game-winner 2:26 into overtime as the Colorado Avalanche rallied past the Edmonton Oilers 4-3 on Friday.
The Avalanche, who won their fifth straight, were on the power play and pulled goaltender Patrick Roy for an extra attacker in the final minute of the third period.
Valeri Kamensky's shot off a scramble went behind the net but Claude Lemieux retrieved it and set up Sakic, who put the puck just inside the left goalpost for his 16th goal of the season.
Colorado, which is 7-0-1 in its last eight meetins with the Oilers, dominated the overtime, collecting all six shots.

Sakic had the puck along the left boards and fed Alexei Gusarov, who pinched in from the point. His shot was stopped in front by an Edmonton defender, but Ricci grabbed the puck in the slot and shot it over goaltender Curtis Joseph for his second goal of the game and ninth of the season.
"I don't think we stole the game at all. We did have 48 shots," Sakic said. "We just keep battling and when we put our minds to it, we'll win our share of games.

"Edmonton's a great team to play against and we always have great games when we play them. They're one of the few teams who're willing to play good hockey anymore and it's great for fans who know and appreciate the way the game was meant to be."

Mike Ricci and Peter Forsberg also scored for the Avalanche, who came back from 2-0 and 3-2 deficits to extend their road winning streak to four games and improved to 15-4-3 against Pacific Division opponents.
Dean McAmmond, Kevin Lowe and Kelly Buchberger tallied for Edmonton, which fell to 1-3-1 in its last five games.

"We wanted to show them we could play with them and we ended up falling just short," said Oilers defenceman Luke Richardson. "They're the Stanley Cup champions for a reason, and they took advantage of the breaks they got."
Colorado went on the power play at the end of regulation when Edmonton's Ryan Smyth was hit with an instigator penalty following a melee with 22 seconds left.

In Hartford, Kelly Chase, Kevin Haller and Steven Rice scored in a 3:04 span of the first period and the Whalers cruised to a 7-2 rout of the New York Rangers, whose winless streak reached a season-high six games.

Keith Primeau, Andrew Cassels, Glen Wesley and Sami Kapanen had the other goals for Hartford, which won for just the third time in 11 games and moved past idle Washington and Ottawa into the final Eastern Conference playoff berth with 54 points.
The seven goals tied a season high for Hartford.
Wayne Gretzky ended his goal-scoring drought at a career-high 21 games for the Rangers, who have scored just eight goals while going 0-4-2 in their last six contests.
In Dallas, Andy Moog made 25 saves for the 350th career win and Sergei Zubov had a goal and an assist to pace the Stars to a 4-2 victory over the Calgary Flames.

Bob Bassen, Mike Modano and Todd Harvey also scored for the Stars, who won for the fifth time in their last seven games and extended their lead in the Central Division to seven points over second-place Detroit.

Jarome Iginla and former Star Dave Gagner scored for the Flames, who are 0-5-2 in their last seven road games. Iginla, a former Dallas prospect, added an assist for Calgary, which is 1-5-1 in its last seven meetings with the Stars.
In Buffalo, Dominik Hasek made 34 saves and Jason Dawe had a power-play goal and an assist as the Sabres ran their unbeaten streak to 11 games with a 5-2 victory over the New York Islanders.
Brian Holzinger, Brad May, Bob Boughner and Garry Galley had the other Buffalo goals. Michael Peca and Michal Grosek set up two scores apiece for the Sabres.
The 11-game unbeaten streak is the Sabres' longest since they went 12 games without a loss in 1980-81.
